newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were mostly firmer at the close on Tuesday, with March Confederate bond futures setting fresh contract highs.
The March Conf rose to 121.00 during the day but pulled back however before the close.
Short-term interest rates, including swaps, were steady, making refinancing of positions at the long end more costly.
"The whole thing is a bit more expensive, since swap rates are stuck, while prices went up in the long end," one Swiss-based dealer said.
He said there was good demand for the 4-1/2 percent Federal 2007 bond, the current benchmark 10-year.
He added prices have largely regained levels seen when the Swiss Treasury last week offered a "mini-tender" of 150 million francs of the June 2007 bond.
The auction, offered at the then-market peak, was five times oversubscribed.
At current levels, dealers expected position-covering for both outstanding longs and shorts. Gains in the Swiss market were seen tied mainly to strength in German Bunds.
March Comi medium-term bond up five at 112.00
Mar Euro Swiss francs steady at at 98.27.
